source_review.notes: Reviewed Bagwell's primary HAMT report, the Steindorfer-Vinju CHAMP and HHAMT papers, current official Clojure and Scala implementation sources, and current Clojure transient, Rust im, and Racket HAMT documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked hash width, fragment width, branching factor, mask/shift/slot/bit/rank, bitmap/array/leaf/collision nodes, CHAMP data/node maps, roots, and reachability notation.
Checked logical slot versus compact index, deep-prefix versus full-hash collision, canonical shape versus object identity, and ordinary hash versus content address remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Complexity expressions include terminal collision work and named hash/equality assumptions.

evidence: Recomputed the bitmap-rank example for slots 2,4,5,7 and index two at slot five.
Recomputed two-bit fragment paths for hashes 0,4,1,2, and 42, including 0/4 second-fragment divergence and the two-entry hash-42 collision bucket.
Recomputed m5/m8 entry sets, beta B→B2 replacement, gamma removal, and identity sharing of collision and chunk-zero branches.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite tuple counts/paths do not measure 32-way/CHAMP object bytes or production costs.

evidence: Verified rank(M,i)=popcount(M & ((1<<i)-1)) from ordered occupied slots and compact children.
Verified association cases for absent, equal-key replacement, unequal deep-prefix hashes, and equal full-hash collision buckets.
Verified removal preserves remaining mappings only under depth-valid leaf/collision collapse rules; arbitrary internal-node lifting is rejected.
Verified fixed-width internal depth ceil(b/w) plus explicit collision-bucket work, and path-copy persistence from immutable copied ancestors/shared siblings.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Hash/equality, layout, persistent update, transient ownership, collision defense, and durability are separate obligations.

evidence: Reviewed empty/singleton, every slot including high signed bit, absent/equal/no-op/replacement, deep shared prefixes, full collisions, collision 2→1, last removal, and bitmap/dense/inline transitions.
Reviewed mutable/stateful/expensive keys/hash/equality, count/shift overflow, transient alias/thread/freeze/failure misuse, refcount/GC/arena retention, and long readers.
Reviewed collision floods, root/version pinning, CAS retries/ABA, malicious graph cycles/bitmaps/counts/fan-out, schema/hash migration, cross-tenant leakage, and crash publication.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Quotas cover keys/values, entries/roots/readers, collision/depth/node/array counts, hash/equality time, transient batches, live/retained bytes, and outputs.

evidence: The executable validates nonempty bitmap/popcount/child arity, every descendant hash fragment at every depth, collision size/distinct keys, and global unique logical keys.
It validates lookup results across nine roots plus old-version replacement/removal/branch isolation and selected untouched-child identity sharing.
The chapter specifies additional dense/CHAMP, cached metadata, transient-owner, lifetime, concurrency, serialization, and durable-root validators.
invariant_checking.notes: The trace covers two-bit bitmap/leaf/collision nodes only, not dense/CHAMP layouts or production key semantics.

evidence: Reviewed unordered-map/hash/equality semantics, fragment/rank derivation, node layouts, lookup, association collision cases, removal normalization, and complexity.
Reviewed CHAMP/bulk layouts, transients/bulk builders, lifetime/failure, concurrent publication, serialization/migration/durability, and security.
Reviewed independent-map, forced-hash, local/global invariant, version/sharing, metamorphic, fault, concurrency, parser-fuzz, and benchmark evidence.
proof_review.notes: Current implementations illustrate practice; no implementation's entire behavior is generalized beyond cited/documented scope.

evidence: Bitmap/rank, path, association, removal, persistence, complexity, transient, and lifetime/publication arguments state separate assumptions.
CHAMP canonicality and bulk complexities are conditional on exact algorithms and layouts.
The finite trace explicitly disclaims 32-way/CHAMP/dense nodes, transients, randomized hashing, concurrency, durability, hostile parsing, and performance proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No fragment width, layout, collision policy, or transient strategy is claimed universally optimal.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact fourteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under Python 3.14.4.
It emits evidence=finite_persistent_hamt_version_trace and reproduces deep-prefix/full collisions, replacement, removal, branching, lookup, layout, and identity sharing.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed draft module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No 32-way/CHAMP/dense/small-map layout, transient, collision flood defense, fault injection, reclamation, concurrency, serialization, crash recovery, parser security, or production memory/cache/GC/tail behavior was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Progresses from hash-map semantics and fragment/rank mechanics through layouts, collision/update/removal correctness, cost, CHAMP/transients, lifecycle, concurrency, storage, security, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed stable key ownership, null/iteration policy, signed shifts/popcount, promotion/demotion and collision nodes, no-op roots, transients/freeze, roots/readers/retention, allocation failure, GC/refcount/arenas, CAS, logical/graph formats, hash/layout migration, child-before-root durability, quotas, faults, and measurements.

pedagogical_review.notes: Derives compact indexing before persistent mechanics, includes a reproducible nine-root forced-hash trace, ten varied worked examples, and five progressive graduate exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Bagwell, Steindorfer/Vinju, Clojure, Scala, Rust im, Racket, hash/security, performance, reliability, storage, formal-methods, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither arbitrary HAMTs, 32/64-bit signed-shift safety, CHAMP/HHAMT/dense/small-map layouts, canonicality, transient exclusivity/freeze, randomized/keyed hashing or collision-flood resistance, mutable-key isolation, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, refcount/GC/epoch/arena correctness, thread safety/linearizability/progress, graph serialization/content addressing/durable crash recovery/GC, hostile-input security, production memory/cache/GC/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
